newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 a tonne lower on Tuesday, as traders expected the market to consolidate Monday's sharp gains.

New York cocoa futures jumped in light, chart-driven dealings on Monday. September rose $33 a tonne, to $1,713, after ranging between $1,720 and $1,665. Spot July jumped $36, to $1,684, while the back months rose $30 to $31.
On the charts, Traders pegged September support near $1,700, with a major downside hurdle seen at $1,650. Resistance was put at $1,722, followed by its life-of-contract high of $1,737.
After Monday's close, CSCE said total open interest in cocoa futures set a new record high on Friday when it reached 105,801 contracts outstanding.
London cocoa futures rallied to new one-year highs early Tuesday, but upward momentum slowed by midday. LIFFE September was up 12 stg at the break, to 1,162 stg, after peaking at 1.169 stg.
